answer: Stamp aggregation: an identity earns rewards only once its score from independent credentials passes a threshold, such as a year-old funded wallet, a paid domain and a verified code account. The verifier checks each stamp's issuer signature and stores a one-way hash, so one credential backs one identity across the whole atlas of members. Each clone must gather its own costly set, since stamps cannot be shared. Limit: stamps can be bought, like aged accounts sold as timber; when audits find an issuer leaking cheap fakes, even an ember of fraud cuts that issuer's weight.
